product_generators.label: Product Generators
product_generators.pitch: Generate ready-to-print products — coasters, keychains, ornaments, pet tags, and more — with one command.

textures.label: Textures & Materials
textures.pitch: Apply procedural and image-based textures to any 3D model. Multicolor, deboss, emboss.

decoration.label: Decoration Tools
decoration.pitch: Batch decoration, template profiles, and auto-multicolor from texture maps.

decoration_learning.label: Decoration Learning
decoration_learning.pitch: Track decoration outcomes, iterate parameters, and roll back to proven recipes automatically.

engineering.label: Engineering Math
engineering.pitch: Real ISO 286 limits-and-fits, beam mechanics with proper factor of safety, and tolerance stacking (worst-case + RSS + Monte Carlo) for parts you actually need to trust. Two-mode UX: plain-English by default, full formula trace and textbook citations when you ask for the math.

drawing_intake.label: Drawing Intake & DFM
drawing_intake.pitch: Hand Kiln a customer engineering drawing and get a per-dimension manufacturability verdict grounded in your machines' measured capability: pass/marginal/fail per characteristic, conservative predicted yield, and concrete orientation / tolerance / compensation recommendations.

print_intelligence.label: Print Intelligence
print_intelligence.pitch: Your printer learns from every print — optimal settings, failure prediction, maintenance alerts.

cloud_sync.label: Cloud Sync
cloud_sync.pitch: Sync designs, settings, and print history across all your devices.

notifications.label: Notifications & Hooks
notifications.pitch: Route VCS events to Telegram, Discord, or a local log — and gate operations with pre/post shell hooks.

teams.label: Teams & Orgs
teams.pitch: Multi-user orgs, team memberships, and fine-grained permission scopes for Business and Enterprise tiers.

design_versioning.label: Design Versioning
design_versioning.pitch: Track every design iteration with mesh diffs, provenance, and full ancestry.

speed_control.label: Speed Control
speed_control.pitch: Real-time printer speed control and layer-based scheduling.

fleet_operations.label: Fleet Operations
fleet_operations.pitch: Drive every printer at once — pause, resume or cancel the whole farm gracefully, fan mid-print changes across machines, and plan material swaps and reroutes for the fleet.

ams_control.label: AMS Control
ams_control.pitch: Start and stop active filament drying on AMS 2 Pro / AMS HT units, with safe temperature and duration guards.

design_modification.label: Design Modification
design_modification.pitch: Change part colors, rebuild designs, and smart AI redesign.

product_intelligence.label: Product Intelligence
product_intelligence.pitch: Smart product generation with proven recipes, QR codes, and batch operations.

provenance_learning.label: Proven Recipes
provenance_learning.pitch: Record and recall proven recipes for any decoration + product combination.

billing.label: Billing & Subscription
billing.pitch: Self-serve Stripe Checkout, customer portal, lost-key reissue, and live license status — for agents and humans.

account_management.label: Account & Sign-in
account_management.pitch: Sign in, sign out, and manage your Kiln account from inside an agent chat — no terminal required.

assembly_manuals.label: Assembly Manuals
assembly_manuals.pitch: Auto-generate flat-pack-style PDF assembly instructions for multi-part prints — exploded cover, bill of materials, step-by-step isometric renders.

part_economics.label: Part Economics
part_economics.pitch: Break sliced plates into per-part time, filament, and cost estimates for quoting, kit pricing, and replacement parts.

engineering_intelligence.label: Engineering Intelligence
engineering_intelligence.pitch: Curated, datasheet-cited Pro+ reference data for parts you have to trust — fastener, hole, and joint specs (ANSI/ISO, FDM-aware clearances, heat-set insert sizing, which joint to use) plus drying advice: whether your loaded filament is ready to print, read against live AMS humidity, and if not, a safe drying recipe in plain English.

material_safety.label: Material Safety & Skin Contact
material_safety.pitch: Honest, cited safety intelligence for what you make — chemical durability and skin-contact suitability for worn or handled parts (rings, bands, grips, earbuds). Free tells you what's risky and when to see a professional; Pro tells you exactly what to do about it and how to prove it. Kiln never fakes a 'skin-safe' claim.

design_inspection.label: Design Inspection
design_inspection.pitch: Structured visual evidence for any design — renders, cross-section slices, raw measurements, and a print-readiness verdict — bundled into one inspectable report with a manifest.

cad_exchange.label: CAD Exchange
cad_exchange.pitch: Move real CAD in and out of Kiln. A design imported from a STEP file keeps its original analytic B-rep and exports it back exactly — true cylinders and planes a machine shop's CAD opens clean, never a tessellated fake.

technical_drawings.label: Technical Drawings
technical_drawings.pitch: Turn any design into a clean, dimensioned production drawing — front, top, and side views with real measurements, a title block, and PNG / PDF / DXF files a machine shop or client can use. Built for selling what you print.

design_session.label: Design Sessions
design_session.pitch: Conversational entry-point — describe what you want to make in plain English, answer a few quick questions if Kiln needs them, then produce an STL that comes with a report of which design checks it passes.

support.label: Support & Feedback
support.pitch: Report a bug or share feedback from inside an agent chat. Free for everyone — server-side moderation, prompt-injection sanitisation, and rate-limiting keep the queue clean before anything reaches the team.

pro.benefits: Everything in Free, plus calibration that learns your printer, mid-print edits, and unlimited textures and decorations.

business.benefits: Business adds team review, approval gates, and 3 printers (grow to 50).

enterprise.benefits: Enterprise adds SSO, RBAC, and audit export.

design_credit.title: Design Credit

branding.title: Branding

co_brand_name.title: Co Brand Name
co_brand_name.description: When set, the cover reads "Made by ``co_brand_name``" instead of the Kiln wordmark.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Ordered list of language codes (e.g. ``["en", "de"]``). Omitted, the manual is English only; unsupported codes fall back to English.

cover_language.title: Cover Language
cover_language.description: Language for the cover; defaults to ``languages[0]`` or English.

background.title: Background
background.description: ``True`` (default) renders in the background and returns at once with ``pending=True``; ``False`` waits for the render inline.

tools.name: derive_assembly_plan
tools.description:
Derive an assembly plan from part GEOMETRY — no hand declaration needed.

Needs Kiln Business.

part_paths.title: Part Paths
part_paths.description: One mesh file per part, positioned as assembled (world coordinates).

part_names.title: Part Names
part_names.description: Display names aligned with part_paths (default: file stems).

assembly_name.title: Assembly Name
assembly_name.description: Cover name for the derived assembly.

material.title: Material
material.description: Default material stamped on each part.

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: Kit shortcut: a design split with tracking. Used only when ``part_paths`` is empty; the plan then comes from the kit's recorded graph instead of measuring geometry.

kit_id.title: Kit Id
kit_id.description: With ``design_id``, which recorded kit to plan. Empty uses the design's active kit; an id the design does not carry returns an error.

pin_recipes.title: Pin Recipes
pin_recipes.description: Optional ``add_pin_joints`` results, each with a ``parts: [a, b]`` pair added, so the plan records the pins on those seams. Used on the geometry path only.

tools.name: diff_assembly_manuals
tools.description: Compute a "what changed" PDF between two manual revisions (Business+).

manual_id_old.title: Manual Id Old
manual_id_old.description: The older manual revision id from manual history. Overridden when a version or release label for the old side is given.

manual_id_new.title: Manual Id New
manual_id_new.description: The newer manual revision id, likewise.

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: The design whose history the version and release labels are resolved against.

version_id_old.title: Version Id Old
version_id_old.description: Resolve the old side as the manual recorded for this design version.

version_id_new.title: Version Id New
version_id_new.description: Resolve the new side as the manual recorded for this design version.

release_id_old.title: Release Id Old
release_id_old.description: Resolve the old side as the manual signed under this release id.

release_id_new.title: Release Id New
release_id_new.description: Resolve the new side as the manual signed under this release id.

release_name_old.title: Release Name Old
release_name_old.description: Resolve the old side by the release's buyer-facing name.

release_name_new.title: Release Name New
release_name_new.description: Resolve the new side by the release's buyer-facing name.

spec_old_path.title: Spec Old Path
spec_old_path.description: Path to the old manual's ``spec.json``; used when no history id is resolved for the old side.

spec_new_path.title: Spec New Path
spec_new_path.description: Path to the new manual's ``spec.json``; used when no history id is resolved for the new side.

assembly_old_json.title: Assembly Old Json
assembly_old_json.description: The old assembly state (JSON string or object). Needed, with the other two render inputs, for the PDF.

assembly_new_json.title: Assembly New Json
assembly_new_json.description: The new assembly state (JSON string or object). Needed for the PDF.

output_pdf_path.title: Output Pdf Path
output_pdf_path.description: Where to write the diff PDF. Without it (or without both assembly states) only the JSON summary is returned.

include_intermediate.title: Include Intermediate
include_intermediate.description: When ``True``, also return the cumulative changelog of every manual between the two. Both sides must resolve to manual history revisions; spec paths are refused. Defaults to ``False``.

include_retired.title: Include Retired
include_retired.description: When ``True``, retired revisions count when resolving labels and building the changelog. Defaults to ``False``.

tools.name: embed_manual_in_3mf
tools.description: Augment a 3MF with the assembly manual + signed manifest (Business+).

manual_id.title: Manual Id
manual_id.description: The manual revision to embed, from manual history. When given it wins: the PDF, ``spec.json`` and any release recorded with it are used, and ``pdf_path`` / ``spec_json_path`` are ignored.

pdf_path.title: Pdf Path
pdf_path.description: The manual PDF to embed when no ``manual_id`` is given. One of the two is required.

spec_json_path.title: Spec Json Path
spec_json_path.description: Optional ``spec.json`` to embed with ``pdf_path``. Omitted or unreadable, an empty spec is embedded.

release_id.title: Release Id
release_id.description: Optional signed release whose manifest to embed. A release recorded on the ``manual_id`` revision takes precedence; the response says when no manifest went in.

tools.name: find_manual_siblings
tools.description: List sibling revisions of a parametric design (Business+).

manual_id.title: Manual Id
manual_id.description: The reference revision.  All other revisions of the same design with different parameter values come back as siblings.

include_retired.title: Include Retired
include_retired.description: When True, surface retired siblings in the result (audit / portfolio review).

include_self.title: Include Self
include_self.description: When True, the input revision is returned alongside its siblings (useful for a UI that wants the full set with the current row marked).

tools.name: generate_assembly_manual
tools.description: Generate a flat-pack-style assembly manual for a multi-part print (Business+).

assembly_json.title: Assembly Json
assembly_json.description: JSON string of the assembly state, as returned by ``create_assembly`` / ``add_assembly_part`` / ``add_assembly_interface``.

output_dir.title: Output Dir
output_dir.description: Directory to write the PDF + per-page PNGs into.  Created if missing.  Defaults to ``./assembly_manual``.

design_name.title: Design Name
design_name.description: Cover-page title; falls back to the assembly's own ``name``.

label_scheme.title: Label Scheme
label_scheme.description: ``"alpha"`` (A, B, C, ... AA, AB), ``"numeric"`` (1, 2, 3), or omitted to pick by part count (alpha for small kits, numeric for large).

use_llm.title: Use Llm
use_llm.description: When true (the default), step copy is written by Kiln's language model with the deterministic template as fallback; false forces the template generator.

branding.title: Branding
branding.description: ``"prominent"``, ``"subtle"``, ``"white_label"``, or omitted / ``"auto"`` to resolve from the caller's plan.

co_brand_name.title: Co Brand Name
co_brand_name.description: A maker name shown on the cover as "Made by <name>" in place of Kiln's wordmark.  Omit it to keep Kiln's mark.

gate_interval.title: Gate Interval
gate_interval.description: Insert a "you should now have this" verification gate after every N work steps (default 4).  No gates inserted when total work steps <= interval.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Ordered list of language codes (e.g. ``["en", "de"]``); each gets its own section in one PDF.  Omitted, English only.  Supported: en, de, fr, es, it, zh, ja; an unsupported code falls back to English.

cover_language.title: Cover Language
cover_language.description: Override the cover's language (defaults to ``languages[0]`` or English). Useful when the cover should match the customer's locale even if the body cycles through several.

design_name_translations.title: Design Name Translations
design_name_translations.description: Optional dict mapping language code to a localized product name (e.g. ``{"de": "Gelenkleuchte"}``).  Each section renders the matching translation as the cover title; sections without a translation fall back to ``design_name``.  Brand names that should not be translated simply pass an empty/missing dict.

step_overrides.title: Step Overrides
step_overrides.description: Optional dict mapping 1-indexed step numbers (string or int keys) to kit-maker copy overrides. Supported fields: ``action``, ``description``, ``orientation_note``, ``tools_needed``, and ``caution``. Use this when the kit includes a custom tool or a designer-known tactile cue the generic copy generator cannot know.

printer_id.title: Printer Id
printer_id.description: Optional printer id (e.g. ``"bambu_a1"``). When given and a screwed joint threads into a printed part, the parts list carries that printer's self-threading prep (hole sizes, engagement, torque ceiling, lead-in) where Kiln has a curated figure, or a labelled generic starting point; the response adds ``data.hardware_prep``.  Omit it for generic hardware rows.

brief_id.title: Brief Id
brief_id.description: Optional saved-goal id from ``design_session``. When supplied and the brief resolves, the response's ``data`` block gains a ``design_goal`` block with the design's duty / environment / safety notes / operating story so the agent presenting the manual can say "This manual is for a [duty] design intended for [environment]" without re-reading the brief separately.  Future enhancement: a "Designed for" line on the cover page.

work_instruction.title: Work Instruction
work_instruction.description: Optional config that turns the consumer manual into a controlled factory work instruction.  Omit it (default) and the manual is unchanged.  Supply a dict to turn on: configurable part / item numbers on the BOM, per-step fastener torque with its honesty tier (a calibrated figure on a known printer+material, otherwise a "verify on a test joint" feel cue with no fabricated number), a per-step go/no-go inspection check, a build/inspect sign-off on the milestone gates, and a document- control / revision-ECO header (DRAFT-stamped when no change record is supplied).  Recognised keys: ``numbering`` (``prefix``, ``pad_width``, ``separator``, ``start_number``, ``revision_style``, ``show_revision_in_part_number`` — defaults render a clean bare sequence "1","2","3"; an org sets ``{"prefix":"KLN","pad_width":5}`` to get ``KLN-00421``); ``control`` (``doc_number``, ``rev``, ``effective_date``, ``change_reference``, ``approved_by``, ``prepared_by``, ``applicability``); ``inspection`` (bool, default true); ``sign_off`` (bool, default true); ``quantity_overrides`` (``{part_id: int}``); ``prior_build_advisories`` (bool, default FALSE — opt-in: fold this design's recorded build history into the steps as inspect-with-care warnings.  Off keeps the controlled document deterministic; when history exists the response carries ``data.build_history_available`` so you can ASK the user before turning it on).  The response's ``data.work_instruction`` summarises what was applied.

strict_certainty.title: Strict Certainty
strict_certainty.description: When True (default), refuse to generate unless every step's joint metadata is complete — a shipped manual should never guess. Pass ``False`` for a DERIVED assembly (the ``derive_assembly_plan`` output): inferred steps render with honest DOUBLE-CHECK badges instead of refusing.  This is the documented kit chain — derive_assembly_plan → generate_assembly_manual( strict_certainty=False).

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: Design to record this manual under.  The generated PDF always lands in its durable home — ``~/.kiln/manuals`` — and when a design identity exists (this parameter, or the assembly's own), the generation lands as a revision in the design's manual history (``list_manual_history`` / ``diff_assembly_manuals`` read it back; the response carries ``manual_id``). Omitted on an untracked assembly, the manual still generates — the response says how to track it.  To keep a manual in the cloud, sign the release (``sign_design_release``) and push it (``cloud_push_release``) — the release embeds the manual's fingerprint, so ``verify_manual_authenticity`` can prove any copy against it from anywhere.

version_id.title: Version Id
version_id.description: Design version the manual documents (default: the PDF fingerprint prefix, the same fallback the auto-trigger path records).

printer_id.title: Printer Id

sign_off_result.description: ``"pass"`` (default), ``"fail"`` or ``"conditional"``. Any other value is recorded as ``"conditional"``.

observed_defects.title: Observed Defects
observed_defects.description: Optional list of defects seen at the go/no-go checks, each ``{step_number, part_id, defect, disposition}`` with ``disposition`` one of ``reject`` (scrap/rework), ``note`` (watch) or ``accept`` (seen and cleared); an unknown disposition is recorded as ``note``.

manual_revision.title: Manual Revision

build_class.title: Build Class

operator.title: Operator
operator.description: Optional name of the person who did the build, stored as given.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Optional free-text notes, kept locally and never sent to the shared corpus.

printer_model.title: Printer Model
printer_model.description: Optional printer model; sets the printer family bucket for the opt-in shared corpus rows only.

joints.title: Joints
joints.description: Optional ``part_id -> joint_type`` map. Required for any opt-in shared corpus contribution; omitted, nothing is contributed.

applied_fixes.title: Applied Fixes
applied_fixes.description: Optional ``part_id -> fix`` map of the corrective action taken, for the opt-in shared corpus rows.

obj_path.title: Obj Path
obj_path.description: Path to OBJ file with UV coordinates and texture.

n_colors.title: N Colors
n_colors.description: Number of color zones (= AMS/MMU slot count). Default 4.

texture_path.title: Texture Path
texture_path.description: Override texture file path (otherwise read from MTL).

output_dir.title: Output Dir
output_dir.description: Output directory. Default: auto-generated temp dir.

min_island_faces.title: Min Island Faces
min_island_faces.description: Minimum faces to keep a color island. Default 3.

min_island_area_mm2.title: Min Island Area Mm2
min_island_area_mm2.description: Minimum area (mm²) for a color island. Default 1.0.

compose_3mf.title: Compose 3Mf
compose_3mf.description: Compose a multi-color 3MF from split STLs. Default True.

printer_id.title: Printer Id
printer_id.description: Optional printer ID.  Validates n_colors against the AMS/MMU slot count, and names the plate the composed 3MF is placed on so an off-bed split lands on the real bed.

tools.name: auto_recess_pocket
tools.description: Add recessed pocket to a face for bed-safe decoration (Pro).

face.title: Face
face.description: Which face to recess: ``"bottom"`` (the default), ``"top"``, ``"front"``, ``"back"``, ``"left"`` or ``"right"``.

pocket_depth_mm.title: Pocket Depth Mm
pocket_depth_mm.description: How deep the pocket should be (default 1.2mm).

pocket_inset_mm.title: Pocket Inset Mm
pocket_inset_mm.description: Rim width around the pocket edge (default 3mm).

output_path.title: Output Path
output_path.description: Output STL path. Auto-generated if omitted.

tools.name: batch_decorate
tools.description: Apply the same decoration to multiple models (Pro).

model_paths.title: Model Paths
model_paths.description: The models to decorate (STL or OBJ), one path each.

content.title: Content
content.description: What to put on each surface: a PNG/JPG/SVG image path, ``"text:..."`` for text, or ``"qr:..."`` for a QR code.

face.title: Face
face.description: Which face to decorate on each model.  ``"auto"`` (default) picks the largest flat face per model; also ``"top"``, ``"bottom"``, ``"front"``, ``"back"``, ``"left"``, ``"right"``, or, on a sketch-built part whose recipe sits beside the mesh, the sketch's own wall name (``"side:l2"``), which follows the wall through a resize and rebuild.

depth_mm.title: Depth Mm
depth_mm.description: Emboss/deboss depth in mm.  0 (default) picks a depth for *material*.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: ``"deboss"`` (cut into the surface, default) or ``"emboss"`` (raised above it).

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Share of the face the decoration covers, 0.0-1.0 (default 0.7).

material.title: Material
material.description: Material the depth is tuned for (default ``"PLA"``).

output_dir.title: Output Dir
output_dir.description: Folder for the decorated files.  Left out, a fresh temporary folder is used.

tools.name: estimate_batch_cost
tools.description: Estimate total cost for a batch of decorated items (Pro).

num_units.title: Num Units
num_units.description: Number of units in the batch.

decoration_cost.title: Decoration Cost
decoration_cost.description: The answer ``estimate_decoration_cost`` gave for one item, passed back as it came.

tools.name: estimate_decoration_cost
tools.description: Estimate cost impact of decorating a model (Pro).

decorated_model_path.title: Decorated Model Path
decorated_model_path.description: The same model with the decoration (STL).

material.title: Material
material.description: Filament the model prints in (default "PLA"); sets the density the extra volume is weighed with.

material_cost_per_kg.title: Material Cost Per Kg
material_cost_per_kg.description: What that filament costs per kg (default 20).

printer_power_watts.title: Printer Power Watts
printer_power_watts.description: The printer's average draw in watts (default 150).

labor_minutes.title: Labor Minutes
labor_minutes.description: Hands-on minutes the decoration adds per item (default 0).

tools.name: find_closest_filaments
tools.description: Which filaments could I buy for this color? Call ONLY when the person asks. Up to three per color, from different makers.

colours.title: Colours
colours.description: Up to 16 hex color codes or color names.

material.title: Material
material.description: The print's material family, e.g. ``"PETG"`` (``"PLA"`` also keeps PLA+ and PLA-CF).  Empty keeps the PLA family and the answer says so in ``material_note``; ``"any"`` looks across every material.

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Keep one maker's filaments, e.g. ``"Bambu Lab"``. Empty for every maker.

finish.title: Finish
finish.description: Empty (or ``"plain"``) for plain and matte filaments; otherwise one special finish: ``silk``, ``metallic``, ``glitter``, ``pearl``, ``translucent``, ``neon``, ``glow``, ``marble_wood``, ``color_shift`` or ``multicolor``.

content.title: Content

output_dir.title: Output Dir
output_dir.description: Folder the heightmap (``qr_heightmap.dat``) is written to.

target_size_mm.title: Target Size Mm
target_size_mm.description: How wide the code will be printed, in mm.  Give it and the answer says whether the code will still scan at that size; leave it at 0 to get the heightmap alone.

nozzle_mm.title: Nozzle Mm
nozzle_mm.description: Nozzle diameter the scan check is judged for.  Leave it out to use the nozzle on record for your printer (else 0.4); the answer's ``nozzle`` block says which size it used.

tools.name: paint_mesh_regions
tools.description: Paint mesh regions by name or id and write a painted 3MF. Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

assignments.title: Assignments
assignments.description: ``{surface: "#rrggbb"}`` — surface by id, by name, or by a plain word (above).  Unassigned regions stay unpainted (the body colour).  At most 16 distinct colours — a painted 3MF carries no more.

crease_deg.title: Crease Deg
crease_deg.description: Crease angle in degrees: pass the value ``segmentation_params`` returned, so the regions painted are the ones shown.  Omitted, Kiln's shared crease angle is used.

min_region_area_frac.title: Min Region Area Frac
min_region_area_frac.description: Smallest region kept, as a fraction of the mesh's surface area: pass the value ``segmentation_params`` returned.  Omitted, the default is used.

partition_hash.title: Partition Hash
partition_hash.description: From ``segmentation_params``.  Checked against the partition this call derives, so approving one set of regions and painting another is a refusal rather than a wrong answer.  Omitting it skips the check.

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: Land the painted result in this design's version lineage, so a paint is a version you can branch, diff, release and roll back like any other change.

branch_name.title: Branch Name
branch_name.description: Branch to put that version on.

printer_id.title: Printer Id
printer_id.description: Check the requested colours against what this printer actually has loaded, and say so when it has fewer.  Advice only — it never blocks a paint.  It also names the bed the painted 3MF is placed on, so a model sitting off the plate is centred on the machine's real bed.

tools.name: resolve_template_decoration
tools.description: Resolve decoration settings for a template, merging profile defaults with overrides (Pro).

material.title: Material
material.description: Material for depth resolution.

depth_mm.title: Depth Mm
depth_mm.description: Override depth in mm (0 = use profile default).

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Decoration mode override — ``emboss`` (raised) or ``deboss`` (carved in); empty uses the template profile's recommended mode.

image_style.title: Image Style
image_style.description: Override image style (empty = use profile default).

tools.name: segment_mesh_regions
tools.description: Split a mesh into paintable surface regions and show them.

input_path.title: Input Path
input_path.description: STL, 3MF, OBJ or any mesh trimesh reads.

crease_deg.title: Crease Deg
crease_deg.description: Dihedral angle above which an edge bounds a region.  Defaults to Kiln's shared crease angle.  Lower finds more, smaller regions; higher merges them.

max_regions.title: Max Regions
max_regions.description: Coarsen until at most this many regions remain.  Omit for the mesh's natural partition.

min_region_area_frac.title: Min Region Area Frac
min_region_area_frac.description: Confetti floor, as a fraction of total area.  Both tools take it so the ``segmentation_params`` this call reports can be handed straight back to either of them and reproduce this exact partition.

partition_hash.title: Partition Hash
partition_hash.description: Accepted and ignored, so the whole ``segmentation_params`` bundle can be splatted into either tool.  This call always mints its own from what it derives.

include_face_map.title: Include Face Map
include_face_map.description: Also return the full face→region mapping (``face_map``: one int per input triangle, packed little-endian int32 and base64-encoded, in the input file's own triangle order).  For apps that draw the mesh themselves and let the user click a region on it.  Off by default — the map says nothing a person can read, and at the face ceiling it adds ~1.6 MB to the response.

tools.name: smart_decorate
tools.description: Intelligent decoration with auto-fix for printability (Pro). Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

model_path.title: Model Path
model_path.description: Path to the STL model to decorate.

content.title: Content
content.description: What to put on the surface: an image or SVG path, ``"text:..."`` for text, or ``"qr:..."`` for a QR code.

face.title: Face
face.description: Which face to decorate.  ``"auto"`` (default) picks the largest flat face; also ``"top"``, ``"bottom"``, ``"front"``, ``"back"``, ``"left"``, ``"right"``, a sketch-built part's own wall name (``"side:l2"``), or ``"wall"`` to wrap text or a line-art mark around the round wall of a cup, jar or vase.

depth_mm.title: Depth Mm
depth_mm.description: Emboss/deboss depth in mm.  0 (default) picks a depth for *material*; a depth too shallow for it is raised and said.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: ``"deboss"`` (cut in, default) or ``"emboss"`` (raised). ``face="wall"`` is deboss only.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Share of the face the decoration covers, 0.0-1.0 (default 0.7).  A QR too small to scan at this scale is enlarged.

material.title: Material
material.description: Material the depth is judged for (default ``"PLA"``).

offset_x_mm.title: Offset X Mm
offset_x_mm.description: Move the decoration across the face, in mm (default 0).

offset_y_mm.title: Offset Y Mm
offset_y_mm.description: Move the decoration along the face, in mm (default 0).

absolute_size_mm.title: Absolute Size Mm
absolute_size_mm.description: ``face="wall"`` only: the size in mm instead of a share of the wall (letter height for text, width for a mark). 0 (default) uses *scale*.

image_style.title: Image Style
image_style.description: ``face="wall"`` only: ``"stencil"`` or ``"logo"`` to carve an image as a line-art mark; ``"auto"`` (default) tells a mark from a photo by looking.

tools.name: inspect_design
tools.description:
Render and analyze a 3D mesh — shaded previews, cross-section slices, raw measurements (volume, watertightness, dimensions), and an optional print-readiness verdict. Channels are opt-in, results land in a manifest.json bundle.

Free accounts get 3 inspections a month; Pro has no monthly limit.

mesh_path.title: Mesh Path
mesh_path.description: Path to the STL/3MF/OBJ mesh to inspect.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Channel names to run. Defaults to ``["rgb"]``. Call with an unknown channel to get the available list.

bundle_dir.title: Bundle Dir
bundle_dir.description: Output directory. A fresh temp dir when blank; a named one must be new or empty (``OUTPUT_EXISTS`` otherwise), so an earlier bundle is never written over.

product_type.title: Product Type
product_type.description: Optional product slug (e.g. ``"frisbee"``). When Kiln has angle knowledge for it, channels render the right views for that product, not the generic set.

tools.name: inspect_mesh_view
tools.description: Agent-side inspection camera: still PNG frames of a mesh from any pose, for YOUR eyes.

mesh_path.title: Mesh Path
mesh_path.description: Path to the mesh (STL / OBJ / 3MF / GLB).

pitch_deg.title: Pitch Deg
pitch_deg.description: Camera tilt; negative looks down (view mode).

focus.title: Focus
focus.description: Optional ``[x, y, z]`` to center the frame on.

focus_region.title: Focus Region
focus_region.description: Plain words naming where to lean in, from ``top``, ``bottom``, ``left``, ``right``, ``front``, ``back`` and ``center`` (``"top left"``).  Read only when ``focus`` is not given; empty means none, and an unknown word is refused.

section_frac.title: Section Frac
section_frac.description: How deep into the part the cut plane sits, as a fraction from the camera side (``0.5``, the default, removes the front half).  Read only in ``section`` mode.

tools.name: verify_mesh_measurements
tools.description:
Measure a mesh file against the numbers it's supposed to hit and get back a receipt: what was asked, what was measured, what matched.

Needs Kiln Pro.

mesh_path.title: Mesh Path
mesh_path.description: Path to the mesh file to measure; a STEP file is converted to a mesh first.  A path that is not a file is refused.

measurements.title: Measurements
measurements.description: A non-empty list of entries, one per number to check, each ``{label, measurement, value}`` with optional ``tolerance``, ``origin``, ``why``, ``module`` and (for ``hole_positions``) ``positions``; ``measurement`` is ``bbox_x`` / ``bbox_y`` / ``bbox_z`` / ``volume_mm3`` / ``hole_count`` / ``min_hole_diameter`` / ``min_wall_thickness_mm`` / ``watertight`` / ``single_body`` / ``hole_positions``.  An empty list, or an entry that cannot be read, is refused.

tools.name: change_part_color
tools.description: Change a part's color in a design recipe and re-slice. Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

part_name.title: Part Name
part_name.description: Name of the part to modify.

new_filament_slot.title: New Filament Slot
new_filament_slot.description: AMS/MMU slot index. The part keeps its current slot when omitted.

tools.name: build_organic_mesh
tools.description: Build a freeform/organic mesh from a smooth-blended primitive recipe. Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link). MAKE DOORS: start with `design_session`, Kiln's front door for making an object — it keeps the goal (what was asked, the numbers settled, the picture shown, what was ruled out) and every make against it, and on Kiln Pro checks the result against that goal. Then make here with `brief_id` set to the goal_id it returned, so this result joins the goal; an imported or downloaded part joins the same way.

recipe.title: Recipe
recipe.description: The recipe as a JSON object: ``name``, ``resolution`` (grid cells across the longest axis, 40-280), optional ``smooth_mm`` / ``mirror`` / ``shell_mm``, and ``primitives``, a list of ``{"type": ..., ...}`` entries (sphere, ellipsoid, capsule, tapered_capsule, torus, arc, rounded_box, ring_stack) with the per-type fields and per-primitive options the tool description lays out.

output_path.title: Output Path
output_path.description: Optional STL output path for the single-mesh mode.  Omitted, the mesh lands at ``<system temp>/kiln_organic/<recipe name>.stl`` (an anonymous temp file when the recipe names nothing usable); the same name overwrites, which is what iterating on one subject should do.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: When True, emit one solid per primitive ``"group"`` + run the fit check + return an assembled preview.

output_dir.title: Output Dir
output_dir.description: Optional directory for the per-part STLs when ``parts=True``.  Omitted, the set lands in ``<system temp>/kiln_organic/<recipe name>/`` — for the same reason ``output_path`` has a guessable default: a part set is the slowest build here and the likeliest to outrun the call.  Either way the directory holds one ``<group>.stl`` per part plus ``_assembled.stl``, the assembled preview, which is kept beside its own parts rather than orphaned in a temp file.

reference_images.title: Reference Images
reference_images.description: Path (or list of paths) to the image(s) the user is asking you to reproduce.  Pass on every iteration, not just the first.

brief_id.title: Brief Id
brief_id.description: The saved goal's id from ``design_session``, so this make is recorded against the goal and checked against it. Empty when there is no goal.

tools.name: design_session
tools.description: Make, design or create any physical object — a part, a bracket, a box, a holder, a gift — as a 3D model ready to print: Kiln's front door for making, where every make for a person starts. Say what they want in plain English (a specific request goes straight to generate; a vague one gets a quick question or two), then generate the STL from OpenSCAD you write (scad_code), with a report of which design checks it passes; every other make tool is a path this one routes to, and takes this goal's goal_id. Verbs: start, update, save, generate.

verb.title: Verb
verb.description: The move to make: ``start``, ``update``, ``save`` (or ``commit``) and ``generate`` (or ``make``); any other word is refused.

idea.title: Idea
idea.description: What the person wants to make, in their words.  Required for ``start``; ignored by the other verbs.

goal_id.title: Goal Id
goal_id.description: The goal ``start`` returned.  Required for every verb but ``start``, and for recording numbers, pictures or refusals on a later call.

answers.title: Answers
answers.description: Replies to the goal's open questions, mapping each question's text to the answer.  Read by ``update``, ``save`` and ``generate``; answers given on ``save`` or ``generate`` are named back under ``assumed``.

override_prompt.title: Override Prompt
override_prompt.description: For ``generate``: an edited generation prompt to use instead of the one Kiln builds from the goal.  Omitted, Kiln's own.

target_size_mm.title: Target Size Mm
target_size_mm.description: For ``start``: a size hint in millimetres, kept with the goal; it does not answer the sizing question on its own.

material.title: Material
material.description: For ``start``: the material the person has in mind, such as ``PLA``.  Empty means none was named.

scad_code.title: Scad Code
scad_code.description: For ``generate``: the OpenSCAD source to compile and check.  Empty asks a configured cloud backend, or hands back the design details for you to write it.

artifact_type.title: Artifact Type
artifact_type.description: The kind of thing being saved: ``design`` (the default), ``feature`` or ``decoration``, stamped on the goal.

spec_numbers.title: Spec Numbers
spec_numbers.description: Dimensions settled in conversation, one entry each, with ``label``, ``measurement`` (``bbox_x`` / ``bbox_y`` / ``bbox_z`` / ``volume_mm3`` / ``hole_count`` / ``min_hole_diameter``, or a name Kiln will learn to measure), ``value``, ``origin`` (``"user_stated"`` or ``"kiln_derived"``) and ``why`` (one plain sentence); ``tolerance`` and ``stated_text`` optional.  Works with every verb; a later entry with the same label replaces the earlier one.

reference_images.title: Reference Images
reference_images.description: A picture the person showed you: an image file path, or a list of them.  Kept on the goal, so every later ``generate`` is checked against it.

decided_against.title: Decided Against
decided_against.description: What the person turned down, as a list of ``{what, why}`` entries kept on the goal; ``{what, withdrawn: true}`` takes one off the list.

material_change.title: Material Change
material_change.description: For ``update``, ``save`` and ``generate``: the filament the goal's part is made in now, as ``{material, why, decided_by, printer_model}``.  Only ``material`` is required; ``why`` is why the old filament was set aside, ``decided_by`` is ``"person"`` when they chose it or ``"agent"`` when you did, and ``printer_model`` the printer it is printed on.  The goal's old filament stays on its history.

annotations.title: Make, design or create an object

tools.name: list_design_goals
tools.description: List your saved design sessions (saved goals).

filter_status.title: Filter Status
filter_status.description: ``"all"`` returns every session; ``"needs_questions"`` only sessions still in the Q&A phase; ``"ready_to_generate"`` committed sessions with nothing made yet; ``"checks_passed"`` / ``"checks_missed"`` / ``"not_fully_checked"`` made sessions by their LATEST making's measured result. ``"matches_what_you_asked_for"`` is the deprecated pre-reading spelling and filters like ``"checks_passed"``.

Sign and persist an immutable named release of a version.

Needs Kiln Pro.

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: Id of the design the release belongs to.

version_id.title: Version Id
version_id.description: Id of the design version being released.  Its geometry, lineage and outcomes are read from Kiln's record.

name.title: Name
name.description: The release name, e.g. ``1.0.0`` (semver), ``2026.4.16`` (calendar) or any other text (arbitrary).  A name already used for this design is refused.

mesh_fingerprint.title: Mesh Fingerprint
mesh_fingerprint.description: Optional echo of the version's mesh fingerprint.  Omit it to sign Kiln's own reading; a value that disagrees is refused (``FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH``).

ancestry.title: Ancestry
ancestry.description: Optional echo of the version's lineage, as version ids from root to this version.  Omit it to sign the recorded lineage; a list that disagrees is refused (``ANCESTRY_MISMATCH``).

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.description: Optional echo of the print outcomes recorded against the version.  Omit it to sign the record; a list that disagrees is refused (``OUTCOMES_MISMATCH``).

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: Your own metadata to carry in the signed manifest. Keys Kiln writes itself (``assembly_manual``, ``spec_receipt``, ``reference_grade``) are dropped and named in ``discarded_provenance_keys``.

branch_name.title: Branch Name
branch_name.description: Name of the branch the version was released from, recorded in the manifest.  Omit it to record none.

signed_by.title: Signed By
signed_by.description: Who signs, recorded as the signer.  Omit it to use the caller's own identity: on Kiln's servers the signed-in account (a different name is refused), locally the declared operator or the computer's user name.

assembly_json.title: Assembly Json
assembly_json.description: The assembly state, as returned by ``create_assembly`` / ``add_assembly_part`` / ``add_assembly_interface`` (JSON text or the object).  When given, an assembly manual is made and its hash signed into the release; when the manual cannot be made for this caller the release signs without one and ``assembly_manual`` says why.  Omit it for no manual.

manual_branding.title: Manual Branding
manual_branding.description: How Kiln's mark appears on the manual: ``"prominent"``, ``"subtle"``, ``"white_label"`` or ``"auto"``. Omit it for ``auto``, which follows the caller's plan.  Used only with ``assembly_json``.

manual_co_brand_name.title: Manual Co Brand Name
manual_co_brand_name.description: A maker name to show on the manual's cover in place of Kiln's line, where the plan permits co-branding; dropped otherwise.  Used only with ``assembly_json``.

manual_languages.title: Manual Languages
manual_languages.description: Ordered language codes for the manual, e.g. ``["en", "de"]``; each language gets its own parts list and steps in one PDF.  Omit it for one section in English.  Used only with ``assembly_json``.

manual_cover_language.title: Manual Cover Language
manual_cover_language.description: Language code for the manual's cover. Omit it to use the first of ``manual_languages`` (or English).  Used only with ``assembly_json``.

manual_design_name_translations.title: Manual Design Name Translations
manual_design_name_translations.description: Language code to product name, e.g. ``{"de": "Gelenkleuchte"}``, used as the cover title in that language; languages without one keep ``name``.  Used only with ``assembly_json``.

tools.name: verify_design_release
tools.description:
Verify a release's signature and (optionally) its mesh fingerprint, embedded assembly-manual hash, and measured spec record.

Needs Kiln Pro.

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: Id of the design, for a lookup by release name; used only with ``release_name`` and only when ``release_id`` is not given.

release_name.title: Release Name
release_name.description: The release's name, looked up under ``design_id``.

recompute_fingerprint.title: Recompute Fingerprint
recompute_fingerprint.description: When true, also recompute the mesh fingerprint from the stored source and compare to the signed fingerprint — detects tampering with the underlying mesh, not just the manifest.

recompute_manual_hash.title: Recompute Manual Hash
recompute_manual_hash.description: When true AND the release embeds an assembly manual (provenance.assembly_manual present), re-hash the on-disk PDF at ``~/.kiln/release_manuals/<release_id>/assembly_manual.pdf`` and compare to the signed SHA-256.  Detects manual tampering or corruption — proves a customer holding a v1.2 kit gets the EXACT bytes that were signed on day 1, not a freshly-regenerated PDF.  Result fields: ``manual_present`` (bool), ``manual_hash_ok`` (bool or None when the on-disk PDF can't be read).

recompute_receipt_hash.title: Recompute Receipt Hash
recompute_receipt_hash.description: When true AND the release signed a measured spec record, re-read that version's record from THIS machine's design library and compare it to the hash in the signed manifest.  Detects a measured record that changed after it was signed — a verdict edited, a check removed.  Result fields: ``spec_receipt_present`` (bool), ``spec_receipt_hash_ok`` (bool, or None when the record can't be read here), ``spec_receipt_reason`` (why, whenever the answer isn't a plain yes). **Bounds worth stating out loud:** this checks the record against the library on the machine running it — the signer's own. The detailed record does not travel with the release, so a buyer holding only the certificate cannot run this check; what they can verify is the signature and the summary it carries.

tools.name: design_for_load
tools.description:
Will this part carry its load? A verdict with its safety margin.

Needs Kiln Pro.

material.title: Material
material.description: Material id (petg, pla, nylon, etc.) or a filament brand id.  A material with no strength figures is refused by name (``UNKNOWN_MATERIAL``) with the ones Kiln can judge.

application_class.title: Application Class
application_class.description: How much margin the use demands, least to most: "prototype", "internal_fixture", "consumer_product", "outdoor_hardware", "life_safety", "lifting_equipment".  Any other value is refused.

print_orientation.title: Print Orientation
print_orientation.description: "along_layer" — the part bends within the layer planes (a beam printed lying flat): the strong case.  "across_layer" — the load pulls the layer interfaces apart (a beam printed standing upright): the weak case, derated for the material's weaker layer bond.  If unsure which applies, use "across_layer" — the conservative reading.

load_duration_days.title: Load Duration Days
load_duration_days.description: 0 = transient.  A load held for a while is derated for creep, smoothly with duration (no steps: day 364 and day 365 agree); far beyond the measured span the answer says it is an extrapolation.  The verdict says what share of its strength the part keeps for that duration, and reads the allowance at the part's own load level: a part loaded harder than the measurements behind the allowance gets a smaller one, and a part loaded past the heaviest level any measurement covers is not vouched for (the verdict fails and says so).

cycle_count.title: Cycle Count
cycle_count.description: How many times the load comes and goes over the part's life: 1 is a static load; a count in the thousands and up is judged for fatigue as well.

service_temperature_c.title: Service Temperature C
service_temperature_c.description: The temperature the part lives at under load, in degrees C.  Omitted = room temperature, and the verdict says so.  A hotter part is judged at the nearest temperature Kiln has data for, at or above it, and the verdict names both: a hot part is weaker the moment it is loaded and creeps faster after.  Past the data for that material the verdict comes back "unmeasured" (passes is null): it keeps the room-temperature answer so the part can still be sized, says where the data end and which materials are measured there, and asks to hear how the part did if it is printed anyway.  Nothing is blocked.  Naming a filament brand as the material (e.g. "bambu_pla_basic") applies that maker's own softening figure where it is lower.

printer_id.title: Printer Id
printer_id.description: Printer identifier (e.g. "bambu_a1") to look up calibration for.  When supplied, the verdict's confidence_band is modulated by the calibration tier (HIGH narrows, LOW/UNKNOWN widen).

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: The design the part belongs to, if it has one in Kiln.

version_id.title: Version Id
version_id.description: The version of that design being checked. Give the design and version the part belongs to and the verdict is kept with that version, so the history can show what was predicted beside what happened; ``verdict_kept`` says where it was kept, or why it was not, and the answer is the same either way.  With a version, ``extras.field_history.this_version`` counts the verdicts kept for it and the reports of how its prints held.  ``pending_field_checks``, when present, lists printed parts Kiln judged that have no report yet, each with the question to ask.

hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.description: What the part carries besides the stated load, so it is counted: a list of items, each ``{"name": "PCB", "mass_g": 30, "count": 1, "position": "tip"}``.  ``mass_g`` is per piece; ``position`` is "tip" (default: the free end, where it bends the arm most), "mid" or "spread".  A short name Kiln knows a typical weight for ("cr2032", "18650") may leave out ``mass_g``; any other item without one is refused by name (``HARDWARE_UNWEIGHED``), never skipped. Liquid in a container is hardware too: a litre of water is about 1000 g.  Another printed part bolted on is hardware with its own weight.

count_self_weight.title: Count Self Weight
count_self_weight.description: Count the arm's own weight, spread along it, as solid plastic (default True).  Turn off when the arm stands upright or the stated load is not its weight (a sideways push).

upgrade_nudge.headline: Size this part for the load it has to carry.
upgrade_nudge.outcome_preview: Kiln Pro would tell you whether the part carries the load, with its safety margin, and recommend the bracing and joints to carry it.
upgrade_nudge.free_included: General design guidance and safety cautions stay available at every tier.

action.title: Action
action.description: Which operation to run: ``ingest_revision``, ``list_history``, ``get_document_text``, ``create_case`` or ``case_status`` (case-insensitive). Anything else is refused with ``INVALID_ACTION``.

supplier_name.title: Supplier Name
supplier_name.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, required: the supplier as the document names it. It must appear inside its ``identity_spans`` span, which must be verbatim in the text.

product_name.title: Product Name
product_name.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, required: the product as the document names it, verified the same way as ``supplier_name``.

document_type.title: Document Type
document_type.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, required: one of the supported types listed above. Any other value is refused with ``INVALID_DOCUMENT_TYPE``.

document_text.title: Document Text
document_text.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, required: the full text of the supplier document. Kiln stores this exact text and its digest; empty, control-character or oversized text is refused.

identity_spans.title: Identity Spans
identity_spans.description: ``ingest_revision`` only: a mapping from identity field (``supplier_name``, ``product_name``, ``revision_label``, optionally ``document_type`` and ``lot_identifier``) to text quoted verbatim from ``document_text``.

product_form.title: Product Form
product_form.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, optional: the product's form as the operator classifies it. It is part of the document's identity, so different forms are separate documents.

lot_identifier.title: Lot Identifier
lot_identifier.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, optional: the manufacturing lot or batch this document covers (certificates of conformance, lot test reports). When given it must appear verbatim in ``document_text`` and ``identity_spans.lot_identifier`` must quote that span; it becomes part of the document's identity, so certificates for different lots coexist. region.title: Region
region.description: ``ingest_revision`` only: the region the document applies to; part of the document's identity. Omitted, it is ``global``.

language.title: Language
language.description: ``ingest_revision`` only: the document's language; part of the document's identity. Omitted, it is ``en``.

issue_date.title: Issue Date
issue_date.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, optional: the issue date as an ISO date (``YYYY-MM-DD``); any other format is refused. Recorded as caller-asserted, not verified.

source_filename.title: Source Filename
source_filename.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, optional: the name of the file the text came from, recorded with the revision.

source_url.title: Source Url
source_url.description: ``ingest_revision`` only, optional: where the document was obtained, recorded with the revision. Kiln does not fetch or watch it.

reviewed_by.title: Reviewed By
reviewed_by.description: Optional caller-supplied reviewer label. Kiln records it as unverified rather than authenticated identity.

review_acknowledged.title: Review Acknowledged
review_acknowledged.description: ``ingest_revision`` only: set ``True``, together with ``correction_reason``, to store new content under a revision label that already exists. Defaults to ``False``.

correction_reason.title: Correction Reason
correction_reason.description: ``ingest_revision`` only: why the content under an existing revision label is being corrected. Required, with ``review_acknowledged``, for that case; otherwise optional.

supersedes_revision_id.title: Supersedes Revision Id
supersedes_revision_id.description: ``ingest_revision`` only: the ``revision_id`` of the document's currently active revision. Required whenever one is active; any other id is refused.

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: ``list_history`` only: the document whose revisions to list. May be omitted when ``document_revision_id`` is given; if both are given they must name the same document.

document_revision_id.title: Document Revision Id
document_revision_id.description: ``list_history``: a revision whose document's history to list. ``get_document_text``, required: the revision whose stored text to return.

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: ``create_case`` only, required: the Kiln design the case is about.

design_version_id.title: Design Version Id
design_version_id.description: ``create_case`` only, required: the version of ``design_id`` the documents are attached to.

document_revision_ids.title: Document Revision Ids
document_revision_ids.description: ``create_case`` only, required: the saved revisions to attach (duplicates are dropped). Each must exist and be active in Kiln; too few or too many is refused.

manual_id.title: Manual Id
manual_id.description: ``create_case`` only, optional: a Kiln assembly manual for this design version whose generated BOM is bound to the case.

bom_items.title: Bom Items
bom_items.description: ``create_case`` only, optional: a BOM snapshot the caller supplies, recorded as operator-attested. Used only when no ``manual_id`` BOM is bound.

currentness_attestations.title: Currentness Attestations

purpose.title: Purpose

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: Optional caller-supplied case-author label. Kiln records it as unverified rather than authenticated identity.

evidence_case_id.title: Evidence Case Id
evidence_case_id.description: ``case_status`` only, required: the case to re-check.

fit.description: ``"press"`` (interference, smaller hole than thing — for press-fit bearings, magnets, pins; a heat-set insert is sized by name, see above), ``"transition"`` (slip-fit, downgrades to ``close`` on FDM with a notice), ``"close"`` (snug slip-through), ``"normal"`` (general assembly, default), ``"loose"`` (alignment-tolerant).

wall_thickness_mm.title: Wall Thickness Mm

edge_distance_mm.title: Edge Distance Mm

hole_purpose.title: Hole Purpose

environment.title: Environment

material.title: Material

days_in_service.title: Days In Service
days_in_service.description: Days the part had carried its load when you looked.

service_temperature_c.title: Service Temperature C
service_temperature_c.description: The temperature it lives at; leave out for room temperature.

load_knowledge.title: Load Knowledge
load_knowledge.description: How you know the load: measured, estimated or guessed.

stress_fraction.title: Stress Fraction

load_n.title: Load N

verdict.title: Verdict

environment.title: Environment

conditioning.title: Conditioning

hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.description: What the part carried besides the load: items like {"name": "PCB", "mass_g": 30, "count": 1}, mass per piece in grams (design_for_load's ``record_with`` anchor carries the list it counted). Kept with the report in words; an item with no mass that is not a name Kiln knows a typical weight for is refused.

supplier_fields_json.description: The supplier's declared fields, as a JSON object string or a dict: ``grade``, ``magnetization_direction``, ``dimensions``, ``coating``, ``lot``, ``test_method`` and ``country_of_origin``.  Unreadable JSON is read as an empty packet, so every field reports missing.

max_temp_c.title: Max Temp C
max_temp_c.description: The product's maximum service temperature in degrees C, if known; with a declared N-grade it checks that grade's documented operating ceiling.  Omitted, no heat check.

band.free: Warnings — always free
band.pro: Sizing and fit for the hardware you bought

tools.name: add_feature_during_print_fleet

feature.title: Feature

printers.title: Printers
printers.description: Required, non-empty: one spec dict per paused printer, as described above. Names must be unique (an entry without one is ``"default"``); duplicates are refused.

first_layer_height_mm.title: First Layer Height Mm
first_layer_height_mm.description: First-layer height of the sliced feature, resting on each paused print's top face. Defaults to 0.2.

hotend_temp.title: Hotend Temp
hotend_temp.description: Nozzle temperature for every printer's resume. Unset, each printer uses its own print's, read off its G-code.

bed_temp.title: Bed Temp
bed_temp.description: Bed temperature, read and checked the same way as ``hotend_temp``.

filament_type.title: Filament Type
filament_type.description: The prints' material, applied to every printer. Unset, Kiln reads each print's own; a printer whose print names none is refused.

parent_design_id.title: Parent Design Id
parent_design_id.description: Optional design these prints derive from, recorded in each session's provenance.

annotations.title: Add a feature across the fleet

tools.name: assess_fleet_power_loss
tools.description: Triage a whole fleet after a power loss — mixed brands/models (Business+).

failures.title: Failures
failures.description: ``{printer_name: failure_id}`` for the affected printers (from ``detect_print_failure`` per printer).  Scopes the triage and enables per-Klipper probe suggestions.  Omit to assess every registered printer (no suggestions).

tools.name: decorate_during_print_fleet
tools.description: Apply the same decoration to N paused printers at once (Business+).

decoration.title: Decoration
decoration.description: Plain-language spec string (``photo:``, ``logo:``, a texture name, or a description), applied to every printer.

printers.title: Printers
printers.description: Required, non-empty: one spec dict per paused printer, as described above. Names must be unique (an entry without one is ``"default"``); duplicates are refused.

depth_mm.title: Depth Mm
depth_mm.description: Deboss depth in mm, (0, 5], the same on every printer. Defaults to 1.2.

image_scale.title: Image Scale
image_scale.description: 0.0-1.0, what fraction of each top face the image fills. Defaults to 0.7.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: Heightmap value above which a pixel is carved away (0.0-1.0). Defaults to 0.35.

bevel.title: Bevel
bevel.description: Slant the carved walls over the top layers for cleaner edges. Defaults to ``True``.

aspect_policy.title: Aspect Policy
aspect_policy.description: ``"auto_crop"`` (default), ``"auto_scale"`` or ``"strict"``: how to handle an aspect mismatch between the image and the top face.

hotend_temp.title: Hotend Temp
hotend_temp.description: Nozzle temperature for every printer's resume. Unset, each printer uses its own print's, read off its G-code.

bed_temp.title: Bed Temp
bed_temp.description: Bed temperature, read and checked the same way as ``hotend_temp``.

filament_type.title: Filament Type
filament_type.description: The prints' material, applied to every printer. Unset, Kiln reads each print's own; a printer whose print names none is refused.

parent_design_id.title: Parent Design Id
parent_design_id.description: Optional design these prints derive from, recorded in each session's provenance.

tools.name: evaluate_fleet_reroute
tools.description: Decide whether a failed FDM job should move to another printer (Business+).

failure_id.title: Failure Id
failure_id.description: ID returned by ``detect_print_failure``. The original printer + failure_type are read from the stored failure report.

alternative_printers.title: Alternative Printers
alternative_printers.description: List of candidate printer dicts. Each must include ``printer_id``; optional fields: ``is_idle`` (default True), ``supported_materials`` (list of material strings), ``build_volume_mm`` (3-tuple of floats; auto-resolved from ``printer_id`` for supported models when omitted), ``success_rate`` (0.0–1.0 from learning engine). Empty list returns a NO_ALTERNATIVES blocked decision.

completion_pct.title: Completion Pct
completion_pct.description: How far the failed print got (0.0–1.0).  A print that had barely started is restarted on the same machine rather than moved; the decision says which way it went.

material.title: Material
material.description: Material the job needs (e.g. ``"pla"``, ``"petg"``).  Candidates whose ``supported_materials`` doesn't include this are filtered out.  Empty string disables material matching.

model_size_mm.title: Model Size Mm
model_size_mm.description: Optional ``[x, y, z]`` model envelope in mm.  Candidates whose explicit or auto-resolved ``build_volume_mm`` is too small on any axis are filtered out.

tools.name: fleet_cancel
tools.description: Cancel prints across the whole fleet, gracefully (Business).

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which printers to cancel.  Omit for every registered machine (each physical machine once).

preserve_temperatures.title: Preserve Temperatures
preserve_temperatures.description: Hold each machine's pre-cancel temperatures after the cancel (staged-swap workflows).

tools.name: fleet_colour_match
tools.description: Which of my printers already has each of these colours loaded, and which one to print on (Business).

colours.title: Colours
colours.description: Up to 16 hex colour codes.  Anything that is not a colour code is listed under ``ignored``.

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which machines.  Omit for every registered machine (each physical machine once).  A name that is not registered is listed under ``not_registered`` and not read.

material.title: Material
material.description: The print's material, e.g. ``"PETG"``.  A spool on record of a clearly different plastic is not counted as owned for this print, and it is kept on ``plan`` so a yes to its offer asks ``find_closest_filaments`` within it.  Loaded spools are matched by colour, the way the planner matches a colour, and each names its own material.

tools.name: fleet_hardware_stops
tools.description: Every printer waiting for a nut, magnet or bearing, in the order to walk the floor (Business).

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which printers to read.  Omit for every registered machine, each physical machine once.

annotations.title: Which printers need hands for hardware

tools.name: fleet_nozzle_agreement
tools.description: Which registered machines disagree with Kiln's nozzle record, and which matter first (Business).

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which machines.  Omit for every registered machine (each physical machine once).  A name that is not registered is listed under ``not_registered`` and not swept.

tools.name: fleet_pause
tools.description: Pause printing across the whole fleet, gracefully (Business).

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which printers to pause.  Omit for every registered machine (each physical machine once, even when it is registered under two names).

keep_temps.title: Keep Temps
keep_temps.description: True (the default) holds each bed at temperature and settles each nozzle during the pause; False leaves both heaters to the printer's own pause behaviour.

tools.name: fleet_resume
tools.description: Resume paused prints across the whole fleet (Business).

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which printers to resume.  Omit for every registered machine.

force.title: Force
force.description: Send the resume even where Kiln believes the printer is not paused (same escape hatch as ``resume_print``).

tools.name: fleet_set_speed
tools.description: Set speed across all registered printers in the fleet (Business).

percent.title: Percent
percent.description: Target speed as a percentage of the sliced speed (100 = as sliced), applied to every registered printer.  A value outside a printer's own range is refused for that printer, and a printer with fixed speed presets takes the nearest one; the reply says which.

tools.name: fleet_skip_objects
tools.description: Skip failed objects across several fleet printers at once (Business).

printers.title: Printers
printers.description: list of ``{"printer_name": str, "object_ids": [...]}`` — the ids are backend-specific (Bambu label ids, Klipper object names, OctoPrint M486 indices), same as ``skip_print_objects``.

tools.name: fleet_thermal_posture
tools.description: Every registered machine's thermal-runaway protection, and what drifted (Business).

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: Which machines.  Omit for every registered machine (each physical machine once).  A name that is no longer registered reports its last stored reading.

refresh.title: Refresh
refresh.description: Read each reachable machine now (default; machines are read in parallel).  ``False`` answers from stored readings only -- no printer traffic.  On a plain install the computer attached to the printers reads each Klipper machine before the call either way (one configuration query each) and keeps the history itself; Kiln's servers keep none.

tools.name: get_print_before_edit_fleet
tools.description: Get the print from before a mid-print edit on N printers at once (Business+).

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Required, non-empty: one dict per printer with ``printer_name`` and either ``session_id`` or ``engine_output_dir``. A session recorded for a different printer than the one it is filed under is reported as a mismatch rather than returned.

annotations.title: Get each printer's print from before a mid-print edit

tools.name: maintenance_due
tools.description: Which parts are due on which machines -- one list, worst first, across mixed makes.

printer_names.title: Printer Names
printer_names.description: The machines to sweep, by registered name. Omitted, every registered machine (on Kiln's servers, every machine you have records for).  Sweeping more than one machine at once is a fleet feature; a single-machine account is refused and told so.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: The parts to check, by name (``cutter``, ``nozzle``).  Omitted, every part Kiln tracks; an unknown part is refused with ``VALIDATION_ERROR``.

recent_faults.title: Recent Faults
recent_faults.description: Each machine's recent cutter fault codes, a dict from machine name to a list of ``{"code", "at"}`` dicts, filled in by the caller's own Kiln.  Omitted, Kiln reads its local event log (nothing on the hosted server).

tools.name: may_i_print
tools.description: May the caller start a print on this printer right now, and on whose say-so?

printer_name.title: Printer Name
printer_name.description: The name of the printer the print would start on.  An empty name is refused.

file_hash.title: File Hash
file_hash.description: The sha256 of the file's bytes about to print, so a person's approval of that one file can count.  Omitted, only a standing delegation for the printer can answer yes, and a person asking is told to ask again with the hash.

tools.name: plan_fleet_material_change
tools.description: Plan future-object material/color changes across a fleet (Business).

printers.title: Printers
printers.description: One spec dict per printer, as described above. Empty plans every registered printer Kiln can discover.

targets.title: Targets
targets.description: Required, non-empty: one dict per object to change, naming the object and its new material/colour as described above.

trigger_object.title: Trigger Object
trigger_object.description: Optional label for the object the change is keyed to; it is recorded on each device's result and does not change the plan.

plate_number.title: Plate Number
plate_number.description: Which plate of a multi-plate source file holds the objects. Defaults to 1; a printer spec's own ``plate_number`` wins.

source_filament_type.title: Source Filament Type
source_filament_type.description: The material loaded now (the "from" side of the change). Unset, Kiln reads each print's own, then the feeding tray; a printer where none is known needs operator action. A printer spec's own value wins.

source_filament_color.title: Source Filament Color
source_filament_color.description: The colour loaded now, used the same way when judging the transition.

require_ams_match.title: Require Ams Match
require_ams_match.description: When ``True`` (the default), a route is ready only when the printer's material status proves the requested slot, type and colour.

build_artifacts.title: Build Artifacts
build_artifacts.description: When ``True``, prepare local recovery sessions for the devices that are ready. Defaults to ``False``. Refused through Kiln's servers, which only plan.

output_dir.title: Output Dir
output_dir.description: Where prepared sessions are written. Empty uses a new temporary work folder.

execute_ready.title: Execute Ready
execute_ready.description: When ``True``, upload and start the prepared session on each ready device. This acts on the printers. Defaults to ``False``; refused through Kiln's servers.

prepared_sessions.title: Prepared Sessions
prepared_sessions.description: Sessions prepared by an earlier call, keyed by printer name, for ``execute_ready``. Sessions built in this same call are used as well. Refused through Kiln's servers.

upgrade_nudge.outcome_preview: Kiln Business would compare spools and capability across the registered machines and prepare one cross-machine answer.

markets.title: Markets

material.title: Material
material.description: Printed material -- e.g. "PLA", "PETG", "TPU", "ABS", "ASA", "PC", "Nylon", "PP", a fiber-filled grade ("CF-Nylon"), "wood-fill", "metal-fill", or "PEEK". Optional when ``use`` is given.

exposure.title: Exposure
exposure.description: How it touches skin -- e.g. "tool grip" / "stylus" (incidental), "watch band" / "ring" / "earbud shell" (prolonged), "mouthpiece" / "in-ear tip" (mucosal), "implant" / "piercing" (out of scope). Blank takes ``use`` when given, else the more cautious "prolonged".

show_math.title: Show Math
show_math.description: Surface source-free engineering detail (public standards, provenance class, confidence) in the remediation block. Off by default.

use.title: Use
use.description: What the part is for -- e.g. "watch band", "tool grip", "ring worn daily", "earbud shell", "mouthpiece" (the last is refused + referred). Alone, ranks lower-risk materials for it.

band.free: Flags — always free
band.pro: Flags

material.title: Material
material.description: The printed material worn or handled -- e.g. "PLA", "PETG", "resin".

exposure.title: Exposure
exposure.description: How it was used -- e.g. "ring worn daily", "brief handling", "earbud tip". Mapped to the same exposure tiers the suitability check uses.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Optional free text kept for the record. NEVER surfaced to other callers and never used to attribute a cause.

design_id.title: Design Id

Return the current event-subscription config.

Needs Kiln Pro.

tools.name: list_hooks

log_events.title: Log Events
log_events.description: Event types written to the local event log file; ``["*"]`` means every event.  Omitted, the saved list is kept.

webhook_events.title: Webhook Events
webhook_events.description: Event types posted to the webhook URLs; ``["*"]`` means every event.  Omitted, the saved list is kept.

webhook_urls.title: Webhook Urls

webhook_hmac_secret.title: Webhook Hmac Secret
webhook_hmac_secret.description: A shared secret; when non-empty, each webhook post carries an ``X-Kiln-Signature`` header over its body.  Omitted, the saved secret is kept.

disable_telegram.title: Disable Telegram

disable_discord.title: Disable Discord
disable_discord.description: When true, turn the Discord channel off and keep its event list.  False (the default) leaves it as it was.

disable_log.title: Disable Log
disable_log.description: When true, turn the log-file channel off and keep its event list.  False (the default) leaves it as it was.

disable_webhook.title: Disable Webhook
disable_webhook.description: When true, turn the webhook channel off and keep its event list.  False (the default) leaves it as it was.

tools.name: summarize_events
tools.description:
Aggregate counts from the event log over the last *window_hours* — a cheap dashboard for a single node.

Needs Kiln Pro.

window_hours.title: Window Hours
window_hours.description: How far back to count, in hours from now. Defaults to ``24``.

tools.name: tail_event_log
tools.description:
Return the last *limit* events from the local event log.

Needs Kiln Pro.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: How many of the most recent log lines to return. Defaults to ``50``; a value below 1 returns one.

tools.name: delete_decoration

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.description: Echo ``preset_id`` here to execute. Omit on the first call to see the confirmation prompt.

tools.description: Delete a design — retire it (default, recoverable) or erase it permanently.

design_id.title: Design Id

confirm.title: Confirm
