tools.name: apply_geometric_texture
tools.description:
Apply a procedural texture as physical surface relief. Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

Free accounts get 3 textures a month; Pro has no monthly limit.

input_path.title: Input Path
input_path.description: Path to an STL file -- or, with ``surface`` / ``region`` (whole-object coverage), a painted 3MF: the mesh under the paint is carved and the paint follows by surface name, so the result is a painted 3MF too (``output_3mf``, ``painted_surfaces``; a surface the carve renamed is listed in ``paint_dropped``).

texture.title: Texture
texture.description: Geometric texture type -- ``"wood"``, ``"lava"``, ``"alligator"``, ``"snakeskin_python"``, ``"snakeskin_diamond"``, ``"bamboo"``, ``"carbon_fiber"``, ``"brushed_metal"``, or ``"honeycomb"``.  Required unless ``region_textures`` names the textures per region.

depth_mm.title: Depth Mm
depth_mm.description: Relief depth in millimeters.  Leave unset and Kiln decides from the texture's mastered depth and the motif size that actually prints, lifted to a depth the printer can show and capped on walls so the relief stays printable.  The result's ``relief_plan`` says what was chosen and why; ``summary`` is the one-sentence version. With ``region_textures`` a given depth applies to every texture; unset, each texture is decided on its own.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Texture scale multiplier.  The default (1.0) is SMART: motifs keep their material-true physical size (a scale pattern prints the same size on a coaster as on a suitcase), and only a too-small object shrinks the pattern — just enough for a couple of motifs to fit, never below what the nozzle can print (the response carries ``auto_scale`` + a warning when this fired).  Pass an explicit value to override.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: Heightmap resolution in pixels, for the SINGLE-FACE carve only.  Unset adapts to the detected face, fine enough to resolve the smallest groove a nozzle can print and no finer.  Explicit values are honored there (a value above what FDM can print is capped, since finer detail only inflates the mesh).  Under whole-object coverage (``surface=``) it does NOT apply: that engine locks the heightmap to the mesh sampling pitch so the relief cannot alias, and reports the value back as ignored rather than returning an unchanged carve in silence.

face.title: Face
face.description: Target face -- ``"top"``, ``"bottom"``, ``"front"``, ``"back"``, ``"left"``, ``"right"``.  If not specified, auto-detects: prefers top face, falls back to largest.  On a sketch-built part whose recipe sits beside the mesh, the sketch's own wall name (``"side:l2"``) is accepted and follows that wall through a resize and rebuild.

surface.title: Surface
surface.description: OPT-IN whole-object coverage via mesh displacement -- ``"all"``, ``"outside"`` (outward-facing only), ``"walls"`` (vertical-ish), or ``"caps"`` (horizontal-ish).  Every choice covers outside-facing surfaces: a hollow body's inside stays plain, and so does a thin rim (a lip, a tray edge) with the relief easing in below it -- the result's ``left_plain`` says which.  Only valid without ``face`` / ``mark_image_path`` (those imply one face); see the docstring note on its finish vs the single-face carve.

invert.title: Invert
invert.description: Swap which part of the pattern stands out.  Normally the pattern's dark detail is the feature (wood-grain lines get carved/raised) and the rest stays flat; ``True`` flips it so the background becomes the feature instead.  Reach for it when the user wants the "negative" of a texture, or says the raised-vs-flat parts look backwards.  Whole-object coverage only (requires ``surface=``).

symmetric.title: Symmetric
symmetric.description: Sculpt the pattern BOTH ways around the surface instead of only into it (or only out of it).  Default relief is one-sided — it starts at the wall and only cuts in (deboss) or only bulges out (emboss).  ``True`` treats the image's mid-grey as the untouched wall, raising the lighter parts on one side and sinking the darker parts on the other — a fuller, more three-dimensional carved-relief / coin look.  It works both faces, so it needs a bit more wall thickness.  Reach for it when the user wants more depth/dimension, or says a one-sided texture looks flat.  Whole-object coverage only.

smoothing.title: Smoothing
smoothing.description: Softness dial, 0.0–1.0 (default 0.0 = off).  0 keeps the pattern crisp with sharp, defined edges (best for geometric motifs, logos, carbon fiber).  Higher values round the pattern into a soft, gentle relief (best for leather, fabric, organic looks) and also tame a sharp texture that is printing rough.  Reach for it when the user wants a softer or more natural finish.  Whole-object coverage only.

prevent_overhangs.title: Prevent Overhangs
prevent_overhangs.description: Print-safety guard.  Default ``"auto"`` and you should almost never touch it: a texture that quietly makes a model need supports it didn't need before is a defect, not an option, so the guard runs by itself wherever the geometry can actually cause that (a round / organic body, where the surface curves away under the relief).  Flat-faced parts can't produce the failure, so it stays off there rather than shallowing their relief for nothing.  Relief that would tip a surface past the printable overhang angle is eased back; the model's OWN overhangs are always left alone.  ``True`` forces it on (costs some relief depth on steep curves), ``False`` forces it off — only reach for those if the user explicitly asks.  Whole-object coverage only.

projection.title: Projection
projection.description: How the pattern wraps onto the shape (whole-object coverage only).  On every wrap the relief eases in just above the bed, so a raised pattern climbs off the first layer and never overhangs it. ``"auto"`` (default) detects the shape: anything with one closed outline — a cylinder, a box, a tray — gets a seam-hidden wrap around its walls by arc length, so the pattern marches round every corner like a label; a notched or hollow outline gets stable per-face planar mapping.  Right for almost everything, so only override it when the result looks wrong.  ``"planar"`` forces flat per-face mapping.  ``"cylindrical"`` forces the wrap-around (use for an outline auto declines to wrap).  ``"spherical"`` wraps like a globe — reach for it on balls, domes, and ornaments, where the other mappings visibly seam or stretch; pattern compresses a little toward the poles (every globe does).

angle_limit_deg.title: Angle Limit Deg
angle_limit_deg.description: Tighten how much of the object counts as the chosen ``surface`` (``surface="walls"`` or ``"caps"`` only).  The built-in walls/caps split is ~45 deg, so on a rounded shape "walls" creeps well up the shoulder and "caps" spills onto it from above.  Pass an angle and only surfaces within that many degrees of vertical (walls) or of flat (caps) keep the texture.  Reach for it when the user says "only on the sides, not the rounded top", "keep the pattern off the shoulders/dome", or the texture is creeping onto a part of the shape they didn't mean.  ~45 reproduces the default coverage; smaller = stricter.  Pair with ``edge_falloff_mm`` so the tighter boundary fades instead of cutting off.  Whole-object coverage only.

edge_falloff_mm.title: Edge Falloff Mm
edge_falloff_mm.description: Feather the texture's edges, default 0 = off.  Wherever the textured region ends (the walls/caps border, an ``angle_limit_deg`` cutoff, or just above the bed), the relief normally stops at full depth — an abrupt step, like a sticker slapped on.  Pass a distance and the carve instead fades smoothly to nothing over that last stretch, blending the pattern into the plain surface.  Reach for it when the user says the texture "just stops", "ends abruptly", "looks like a sticker", or asks for it to "blend", "feather", or "fade into the surface".  2–5mm reads naturally on hand-sized objects.  Whole-object coverage only.

falloff_curve.title: Falloff Curve
falloff_curve.description: Shape of the ``edge_falloff_mm`` fade. ``"smoothstep"`` (default) eases in and out — right for almost everything.  ``"linear"`` ramps straight (a more mechanical, chamfer-like fade); ``"ease"`` stays subtle longest — the softest, most organic blend.  Only meaningful with ``edge_falloff_mm``.

region.title: Region
region.description: Texture ONE named surface region and leave the rest plain — the same regions ``segment_mesh_regions`` shows and ``paint_mesh_regions`` colours: the region's name ("Outside", "Top rim", "Inside floor"), its id, or the user's own word for it ("the outside", "handle", "lid").  "Honeycomb the outside, leave the rim plain" is ``region="outside"``.  Whole-object coverage is implied (``surface`` narrows it further, default "all"); the relief eases out at the region's edge the way it eases off the bed, so the pattern meets its neighbour with a shoulder, not a cliff.  A word that fits several surfaces refuses with the candidates — ask the user, never guess. The result's ``coverage.region`` names what was textured and ``coverage.left_plain`` what was not, and the output remembers the region so ``paint_mesh_regions`` can still colour it by the same name afterwards.  Can't combine with ``face`` / ``mark_image_path``.

region_textures.title: Region Textures
region_textures.description: Several regions, each with its OWN texture, in one carve: ``{"front": "honeycomb", "back": "honeycomb", "top": "wood"}`` -- keys are surfaces exactly as ``region`` takes them (name, id, or the user's word), values are geometric texture names.  "Honeycomb on the walls, wood on the lid" is one call.  Regions that share a texture share one pattern; every region keeps its own edge ease, the thin-wall clamp sees each texture's depth, and the output remembers every region by name for the paint step.  Leave ``texture`` out (the map names them all). Can't combine with ``region``.

segmentation_params.title: Segmentation Params
segmentation_params.description: The ``segmentation_params`` block a ``segment_mesh_regions`` call returned, passed back verbatim, so ``region`` / ``region_textures`` refer to the exact partition the user was shown.  Optional — omitted, the mesh is segmented at the same defaults that call uses.

mark_image_path.title: Mark Image Path
mark_image_path.description: Optional PNG/JPG of a logo or photo to set into the textured face (see **Layered finish** above).

mark_style.title: Mark Style
mark_style.description: Image processing for the mark -- ``"stencil"`` (bold binary, best for logos; the default), ``"coin"`` (posterized photo relief in a circular medallion), ``"photo"``, ``"medallion"``, ``"portrait"``, or ``"default"``.  Same styles as ``decorate_surface``.

mark_scale.title: Mark Scale
mark_scale.description: Mark box as a fraction of the face (default 0.45); the mark contain-fits inside, aspect kept.

mark_offset_x_mm.title: Mark Offset X Mm
mark_offset_x_mm.description: Continuous placement offset from the face centre, along the face's own width axis (image right), in mm.  Adds on top of ``mark_placement``.

mark_offset_y_mm.title: Mark Offset Y Mm
mark_offset_y_mm.description: Same, along the face's height axis (image up).  The mark's clear panel is clamped to stay on the face after offsets.

mark_depth_mm.title: Mark Depth Mm
mark_depth_mm.description: Mark carve depth (default: the texture's own depth, so the finish reads as one carve).

save_to_library.title: Save To Library
save_to_library.description: If True, save this finish's RECIPE (texture + depth + scale + seed + mode) to the decoration library so the dialed-in look is nameable and reusable -- offer this when the user has tuned depth/scale/seed away from the defaults and likes the result.

printer_id.title: Printer Id
printer_id.description: The registered printer that will print this part.  Its nozzle width sets the smallest motif the relief keeps and its layer height the shallowest relief that prints; both are read from the printer's recorded nozzle (else its model's stock nozzle) and its slicer profile. Unset or unknown: 0.4mm / 0.2mm assumed, and the plan says so.

tools.name: apply_image_texture
tools.description:
Apply a photo-based texture as a tiled deboss/emboss pattern. Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

Free accounts get 3 textures a month; Pro has no monthly limit.

input_path.title: Input Path
input_path.description: Path to an STL file -- or, with ``surface`` / ``region``, a painted 3MF whose paint follows the carve by surface name (see ``apply_geometric_texture``).

image_path.title: Image Path
image_path.description: Path to a texture photo (JPEG or PNG).

tile_size_mm.title: Tile Size Mm
tile_size_mm.description: Physical size of one tile repeat in mm. Default (None) is ONE-SHOT SMART: the motif period is read from the image itself and the repeat sized so motifs print at a size the material can show, as the curated presets are. The response carries ``auto_tile_mm`` + a warning naming the chosen size.  Pass an explicit value to override; smaller = more repeats = finer pattern.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: Max pixels per tile edge before tiling (default 300; higher is capped, since finer detail exceeds what FDM prints).

face.title: Face
face.description: Surface targeting mode: ``"auto"`` — find the largest flat face (current default). ``"front"`` — single flat panel on the front of a cylinder. ``"cylindrical"`` — wrap texture around the full cylinder using *num_panels* flat panels. ``"top"``, ``"bottom"``, ``"back"``, ``"left"``, ``"right"`` — target a specific flat face by name. ``"side:l2"`` — a sketch-built part's own wall, by the sketch entity that swept it (the recipe must sit beside the mesh); it follows the wall through a resize and rebuild.

num_panels.title: Num Panels
num_panels.description: Number of flat panels for cylindrical wrap (default 8, range 4-12).  More panels = smoother wrap but slower compile.  Only used when ``face="cylindrical"``.

style.title: Style
style.description: How the photo becomes a heightmap: ``"posterized"`` (the default), ``"sharp"`` or ``"soft"``, as described under Heightmap styles above.  Any other value is read as ``"soft"``.

surface.title: Surface
surface.description: **Whole-object coverage** — wrap the user's OWN image around EVERY selected surface of ANY mesh (curved, organic, imported — not just flat faces and cylinders) by direct mesh displacement.  ``"all"`` / ``"outside"`` / ``"walls"`` / ``"caps"``; can't combine with an explicit ``face``.  This is the path for "wrap my leather photo around this dragon".  A hollow body's inside and any thin rim stay plain.  The bed-contact band stays flat and thin walls are automatically protected, same as the preset textures.

invert.title: Invert
invert.description: Swap which part of the image stands out (the dark detail is normally the feature; ``True`` makes the light parts the feature instead).  Whole-object coverage only.

symmetric.title: Symmetric
symmetric.description: Sculpt the image BOTH ways around the surface (image mid-grey = the untouched wall) instead of only cutting in or only raising out — a fuller, coin-like relief.  Needs a bit more wall thickness.  Whole-object coverage only.

smoothing.title: Smoothing
smoothing.description: Softness dial 0.0-1.0 (default 0 = crisp). Higher rounds the relief into a soft, gentle finish — best for fabric/organic looks or a photo that prints rough. Whole-object coverage only.

prevent_overhangs.title: Prevent Overhangs
prevent_overhangs.description: Print-safety guard, default ``"auto"`` (leave it alone): relief that would make the model need supports it didn't need before is eased back automatically on round / organic bodies, where that can actually happen, and left alone on flat-faced parts, where it can't.  The model's own overhangs are never touched.  ``True`` / ``False`` force it on or off.  Whole-object coverage only.

projection.title: Projection
projection.description: How the image wraps the shape (whole-object coverage only): ``"auto"`` detects (one closed outline → seam-hidden wrap round the walls, notched or hollow → per-face planar); ``"planar"`` / ``"cylindrical"`` force it; ``"spherical"`` wraps like a globe — for balls, domes, ornaments.

angle_limit_deg.title: Angle Limit Deg
angle_limit_deg.description: Tighten how much of the object counts as the chosen ``surface`` (``"walls"`` or ``"caps"`` only). Only surfaces within this many degrees of vertical (walls) or of flat (caps) keep the texture — reach for it when the user says "only on the sides, not the rounded top" or the image is creeping onto a shoulder/dome they didn't mean. ~45 reproduces the default split.  Whole-object coverage only.

edge_falloff_mm.title: Edge Falloff Mm
edge_falloff_mm.description: Feather the texture's edges (default 0 = off): the relief fades smoothly to nothing over the last N mm before the textured region ends, instead of stopping at an abrupt step.  Reach for it when the user says the texture "just stops", "looks like a sticker", or asks for it to "blend/feather/fade into the surface".  2–5mm reads naturally.  Whole-object coverage only.

falloff_curve.title: Falloff Curve
falloff_curve.description: Shape of the ``edge_falloff_mm`` fade: ``"smoothstep"`` (default, eases both ends), ``"linear"`` (straight ramp), or ``"ease"`` (subtlest, most organic). Only meaningful with ``edge_falloff_mm``.

region.title: Region
region.description: Wrap the image over ONE named surface region and leave the rest plain — the same regions ``segment_mesh_regions`` shows and ``paint_mesh_regions`` colours, by name ("Outside"), id, or the user's own word ("the handle").  Implies whole-object coverage (``surface`` narrows it, default "all"); the relief eases out at the region's edge like it eases off the bed.  A word fitting several surfaces refuses with the candidates.  The output remembers the region so it can still be painted by name. Can't combine with an explicit ``face``.

segmentation_params.title: Segmentation Params
segmentation_params.description: The block ``segment_mesh_regions`` returned, passed back verbatim so ``region`` means the partition the user saw.  Optional.

tools.name: apply_procedural_texture
tools.description:
Apply a multicolor procedural texture (requires AMS/MMU for multi-material printing). Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

Free accounts get 3 textures a month; Pro has no monthly limit.

texture.title: Texture
texture.description: Which color pattern: "camo", "tiger_stripe", "digital_camo", "ocean", "tie_dye", "marble", "lava", "galaxy", or "custom" (your own image via ``image_path``). ``list_procedural_textures`` describes each.

num_colors.title: Num Colors
num_colors.description: Number of color zones / AMS slots (default 4).

image_path.title: Image Path
image_path.description: Your own pattern image as the texture — only with ``texture="custom"``.  The image's tones posterize into ``num_colors`` zones (2 colors on a black/white pattern reproduces it exactly); works with any palette. One-shot: no sizing input needed (see ``image_tile_mm``).

image_tile_mm.title: Image Tile Mm
image_tile_mm.description: Physical repeat size for a custom image pattern.  Default (None) measures the motif period from the image and sizes the repeat so motifs print at a size the material can show, like the curated presets; the response carries ``auto_tile_mm`` + a warning naming the choice.  Pass a value to override.

color_palette.title: Color Palette
color_palette.description: Optional list of hex colors (overrides all). **Keeping a custom look:** when this is the user's own colors (not a curated preset) and they seem happy with the result, offer to save it with ``save_custom_palette`` -- that's what makes it available to ``push_palettes_to_cloud`` later, the same way the web app's explicit "save to library" works.  Ask, don't save automatically; a quick experiment doesn't need to be kept.  The result carries a ``save_this_palette`` hint with ready-to-use call args when this applies.

color_overrides.title: Color Overrides
color_overrides.description: Optional dict mapping semantic role names to hex colors.  Only specified roles are changed; the rest keep defaults.  Example: ``{"foam": "#87CEEB", "deep": "#000033"}``. Use ``list_procedural_textures`` to see available roles.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: Optional name of one of the texture's curated colourways, as ``list_procedural_textures`` lists them.  Used when neither ``color_palette`` nor ``color_overrides`` is given; an unknown name is refused with the available presets.

custom_palette_name.title: Custom Palette Name
custom_palette_name.description: Optional name of a palette saved with ``save_custom_palette``.  Used when no explicit colours or preset are given; an unknown name is refused with the saved names.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Texture scale multiplier.  Larger = coarser pattern, smaller = finer detail.  Default 1.0.

surface.title: Surface
surface.description: Which faces to texture. "all" textures every face (default). "outside" skips interior faces. "walls" only textures vertical/curved faces. "caps" only textures flat/horizontal faces. Filtered-out faces are placed in zone 0 (base color).

save_to_library.title: Save To Library
save_to_library.description: If True, save the texture result to the decoration library for reuse.  The decoration will have ``content_type="procedural_texture"`` and store all parameters needed to reproduce it.

mark_image_path.title: Mark Image Path
mark_image_path.description: Optional PNG/JPG of a logo or photo to carve into the finish (see **Layered finish** above).

mark_scale.title: Mark Scale
mark_scale.description: Mark box as a fraction of the face (default 0.45); contain-fit, aspect kept.

mark_offset_x_mm.title: Mark Offset X Mm
mark_offset_x_mm.description: Continuous placement offset from the face centre, along the face's own width axis (image right), in mm.  Adds on top of ``mark_placement``.

mark_offset_y_mm.title: Mark Offset Y Mm
mark_offset_y_mm.description: Same, along the face's height axis (image up).  The mark's clear panel is clamped to stay on the face after offsets.

relief_texture.title: Relief Texture
relief_texture.description: Optional geometric texture (``"alligator"``, ``"wood"``, ...) to carve as physical relief UNDER the color split -- the stacked finish.  One compile: the relief debosses first, then the color zones split over the carved surface, so the recess walls carry the zones straight through (the same proven carve-then-split path the lava relief and user marks use).  A mark can ride along too; its clear panel composes into the same carve.

relief_depth_mm.title: Relief Depth Mm
relief_depth_mm.description: Carve depth for ``relief_texture`` in mm; unset uses that texture's own catalog depth (what ``apply_geometric_texture`` would cut).

printer_id.title: Printer Id
printer_id.description: Optional printer to check this palette against its loaded filament.  When given, the result carries an ``ams_advisory`` saying whether the design prints true on what's loaded right now -- advice only, never a block.  Read only from that exact printer (or reported as unknown); on the hosted API, where there is no printer, it is always unknown.

tools.name: delete_custom_palette
tools.description:
Delete a saved custom color palette.

Needs Kiln Pro.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the palette to delete.

tools.name: keep_painted_detail
tools.description:
Keep a model's painted-on detail when it prints. Opens Kiln's interactive inline 3D stage on the result (orbit/zoom panel in MCP Apps hosts; hosted sessions add a browser stage link).

Free accounts get 3 textures a month; Pro has no monthly limit.

model_path.title: Model Path
model_path.description: The textured model.  GLB/glTF embed their image maps; models that carry vertex colors instead (vertex paint, photogrammetry and marketplace exports — PLY/OBJ) work through those, speckle-smoothed automatically.  A plain STL carries neither, and a STEP file carries geometry only — in both cases there is no painted detail to keep, and the tool says so.

output_path.title: Output Path
output_path.description: Where to write the STL (default: temp).

target_edge_mm.title: Target Edge Mm
target_edge_mm.description: Surface refinement target (default 1.0 — finer expresses more detail, costs triangles).

invert.title: Invert
invert.description: Raise the dark marks themselves instead of the bright surroundings (see CHOOSING ``invert``).

design_id.title: Design Id
design_id.description: Optional design to track this under — the result is registered as a new version so the original and the embossed variant both stay in history.

tools.name: list_custom_palettes
tools.description:
List all saved custom color palettes.

Needs Kiln Pro.

tools.name: list_procedural_textures
tools.description: List all available procedural texture types, palettes, and presets.

tools.name: preview_texture_2d
tools.description: Render a flat 2D preview of a texture as a PNG image.

image_path.title: Image Path
image_path.description: Path to a photo for image-based mode.

tile_size_mm.title: Tile Size Mm
tile_size_mm.description: Physical tile size in mm (image mode).

output_path.title: Output Path
output_path.description: Where to save the PNG.  If empty, a fresh file in the system temp directory, one per call.  A path that already exists is refused (``OUTPUT_EXISTS``), never written over.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: Name of a built-in preset palette (e.g. ``"woodland"``).

tools.name: push_palettes_to_cloud
tools.description:
Push locally saved custom palettes to your cloud account.

Needs Kiln Pro.

tools.name: save_custom_palette
tools.description:
Save a custom color palette for reuse with any texture.

Needs Kiln Pro.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: List of colors — hex (``"#FF0000"``) or named (``"baby blue"``, ``"salmon"``, ``"forest green"``).

texture.title: Texture
texture.description: Optional texture this palette is designed for.

keep_painted_detail.says: Raised the painted detail into relief

notes.kept: {change} — kept as version {version} of your design “{name}”, after version {parent}.
notes.unchanged: The edit left the file exactly as it was, so there is no new version to keep.
notes.not_saved: Kiln could not save this edit to your history just now; the edited file is below.
notes.ambiguous: This part matches saved versions in more than one of your designs ({matches}), so Kiln did not add this edit to any of their histories rather than guess. Say which design it belongs to, and keep it there.
